### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b4fa6cc9d8295e891d5f8d2264aee1cca36c203` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db8dd24101e3e0cada4a8a87088f8d2a82819c5b` — the merge of head `76d25fa9854e7d8620cb02013943a56e7d69bae5` into base `9b4fa6cc9d8295e891d5f8d2264aee1cca36c203`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db8dd24101e3e0cada4a8a87088f8d2a82819c5b && git checkout db8dd24101e3e0cada4a8a87088f8d2a82819c5b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b4fa6cc9d8295e891d5f8d2264aee1cca36c203 76d25fa9854e7d8620cb02013943a56e7d69bae5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b4fa6cc9d8295e891d5f8d2264aee1cca36c203 && git merge --no-ff 76d25fa9854e7d8620cb02013943a56e7d69bae5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b4fa6cc9d8295e891d5f8d2264aee1cca36c203
```

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, judged RIGHT.** The diff adds one `RefusedStoredShape` to `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES`, a module the header marks internal to `packages/spec` and not re-exported from `conversions/index.ts`. `reportRefusedStoredShapes` runs only when a caller passes an `onTodo` sink (the stored pass and `canonicalizeStoredFlow`); the authoring funnel and the read seams pass none, so no door's accept/refuse verdict moves. `duplicate-global-filter-names.ts` and `dashboard.zod.ts` are untouched (file list: 5 files, none of them). Every other place the sibling id `ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused` is enumerated on the head (changesets, the two entries, the detector, the test) is a place the new id is present too or has no reason to be; no census or ledger enumerates refused-shape ids.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts`** — judged against the refusing door it cites.

- *Same predicate, same inputs.* `DashboardSchema` (`dashboard.zod.ts` line 1869) attaches `checkDashboardReservedDateRangeGlobalFilters` as a dashboard-level `superRefine`, which calls `reservedDateRangeGlobalFilters(dashboard.dateRange, dashboard.globalFilters)` and adds one `custom` issue per entry at `['globalFilters', entry.index, entry.key]`. The detector calls the same function with the same two arguments on the stored body and reports at `${path}.globalFilters[${entry.index}].${entry.key}`. The only way the stored body and the parsed value could disagree on either argument is a default or transform between them: `GlobalFilterSchema.name` is `z.string().optional()` with **no** `.default(field)` (the "defaults to field" in its TSDoc is the predicate's own `filterKeyOf` fallback, not a Zod default), and `DashboardSchema.dateRange` is `strictObject(...).optional()` with no default — so an unnamed entry resolves to `key: 'field'` on both sides and an absent `dateRange` is "not declared" on both. Site and set match; the test asserts the parse's issue paths equal the TODO paths in all three listing cases.
- *No false positive on the controls.* `reservedDateRangeGlobalFilters` returns `[]` when `dateRange` is not a non-null object (control 1: undeclared `dateRange`, keyed by name or by field — parse accepts, nothing listed) and ignores an entry whose `name` is non-empty and not `dateRange` even when its `field` is `dateRange` (control 2: `{ name: 'when', field: 'dateRange' }` — parse accepts, nothing listed). Both controls are pinned beside the parse's `success: true`. A key both repeated and reserved is listed once under the duplicate detector (second declaration) and once per entry under this one — three TODOs, matching the three `custom` issues the parse raises; pinned.
- *Alias spellings are not a gap.* A stored row spelling `filters:` for `globalFilters` or `key:` for `name` is not read by the predicate, but `strictObject` aliases are refused with a prescription, never accepted (`strict-object.ts` header), so such a row is refused by the parse at the alias key, not by this refinement — "listed exactly when that door refuses it" holds for the refinement this detector mirrors, and the sibling detector reads the same way.
- *Collection and walker.* `applyConversionsToStoredItem('dashboard', row)` wraps the row as `{ dashboards: [row] }` via `SINGULAR_TO_PLURAL` (`stored.ts` lines 113–117); `mapCollection(stack, 'dashboards', …)` skips a non-array and non-dict items, and the mapper returns the item unchanged so `changed` stays false and the stack is returned by identity — no rewrite, pinned by `expect(item).toEqual(row)`.
- *Merge with #29589 intact.* The head's file keeps the `fieldPatches` paragraph in the header, the `ObjectExtensionSchema` import, `refusedFieldPatchKeys`, `objectExtensionFieldPatchKeyGrammar`, and `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES` ends `…, dashboardDuplicateGlobalFilterName, dashboardReservedDateRangeGlobalFilter, objectExtensionFieldPatchKeyGrammar`; the roster pin lists all ten ids in that order. The two-dot diff against `origin/main` is the same hunk as the three-dot diff, so nothing of #29589 was dropped or re-spelled.
- *Runtime strings.* The `reason` carries no tracker number (pinned by `not.toMatch(/#\d{3,}/)`); the `from` payload is the reserved key and the index only — no entry body, so no label or option text leaks, consistent with the sibling's "name and the sites only" discipline. The `// ── #29541 …` banner is a code comment in the file's existing style.
- Edge probed and not a finding: `dateRange` set to an array is "declared" to the predicate (`typeof [] === 'object'`) and such an entry would be listed, while the parse refuses the row at `dateRange` itself (invalid type) — the row is refused and loads invalid either way, the refinement is the door's own code, and the shape is not one the schema or any example writes. Noted, no fix asked.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range-refused.ts`** — one sentence added to `acceptanceCriteria`: "`os migrate meta --stored` lists each such stored dashboard under this entry's id, at the entry's `name` (or `field`)." **`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused.ts`** — one sentence added: "…at the second declaration's `name` (or `field`)." True of `dashboardDuplicateGlobalFilterName`, which reports at `globalFilters[indexes[1]].secondKey`. Nothing else changed.

Still `in_progress` at 03:02Z, the last read this record took: `Test Core (2,3,5,6/8)` and `Test UI (9,14,16/16)`. No gate on the head is red. This record judges the tree; the landing rule (every required check green) is the seat's separate precondition — the seat re-reads those seven shards before any ready, queue or auto-merge, and a red among them voids this record's gate reading, not its design judgment.
